title: CanopyX data protocol, version 2 (canopyx/2)
description: Every canopyx/2 document. The schema lists every field of the current revision and rejects unknown ones, so it doubles as a writer check. Readers must ignore unknown fields so documents from a newer canopyx/2 writer still load.

matrixValue.description: A scalar or its display text. Writers and readers check its kind against the declared attribute; datetime values use ISO text and UTC when no zone is supplied.

matrixAxis.description: Writers and readers also enforce unique attribute/item ids and references to declared attributes.

matrix.description: A state matrix with at most one million row/column pairs. Writers and readers also enforce axis sizes, declared state digits, note coordinates and uniqueness, and total-state references.

gridRow.description: A flat row with a dataset-stable identity. Writers and readers also enforce unique identities across the dataset.

fields.description: Values of the view's record fields (record.fields): shown in the record drawer only, never queried, searched, sorted, exported or saved.

gridEditorName.description: text, number, date, datetime, time, select, toggle, lookup, or an editor a plugin or the host registers.

gridEditor.description: The typed editor of an editable column. A name alone is shorthand for { "type": name }; without one the column's kind chooses text, number or datetime.

min.description: Number editors: the smallest value, also the start of step.

step.description: Number editors: Up and Down move by it; values keep its multiple.

options.description: Select choices, or the fixed suggestions of a lookup.

lookup.description: Lookup editors: the column whose values it suggests through the data source, how many and after how many characters.

gridValidation.description: Checks an edited value must pass before its row commits; the runtime's messages are the gridEdit… labels unless message replaces them.

min.description: A number, or an ISO 8601 moment with its time zone for date-and-time columns.

max.description: A number, or an ISO 8601 moment with its time zone for date-and-time columns.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole text must match, in the syntax JavaScript and .NET share.

gridCommit.description: Changed and new rows a grid asks its writer to save: an update carries the new values and the values the reader started from; an insert (op insert) carries every value of the new record under the client's temporary id and no original. The revision is the one the grid read. The writer authorizes and executes each row (docs/data-protocol.md#editing-and-commit).

id.description: The runtime's temporary id of the new row: new-1, new-2, ...

gridCommitResult.description: A writer's answer to gridCommit, per row: saved (with optional canonical cells, and for an insert an optional newId, the stored identity that replaces the client id), error (with a message or messages by column) or conflict. A row the answer leaves out was not saved; revision is the dataset's revision after the commit.

gridLive.description: Live data for a flat grid: rows change in place, keeping the reader's query, selection, focus, scroll position, open drawer and pending edits. stableOrder (default true) keeps rows whose sort keys change in their places until the reader re-sorts; flash marks changed cells (true, or { durationMs }); batchMs applies changes arriving within that time together; pollMs polls the source (a hosted grid's revision-aware refresh, an inline grid's live.load function); announce (default true) announces added and removed rows; pauseWhenHidden (default true) skips polls while the page is hidden.

gridRowUpdate.description: A row update of a gridTransaction: the row's id and the cells to change (a null cell clears it); tone, className, detail and fields replace the row's when given, and null clears tone and className.

gridFacetPanel.description: A facet panel beside (side) or above (top) a flat grid: value lists with counts and ranges with histograms for the columns it names, each counting the result without its own column's conditions. The reader's choices are column conditions of the query; the grid state keeps whether the panel is open. A hosted grid's facets must be reporting facet columns.

gridCalendarEndTime.description: A time of day, HH:mm, or 24:00 for the end of the day.

gridCalendar.description: A calendar of a flat grid's records (docs/calendar.md): each record is an event starting at its start cell, shown in month, week, day, N-day, agenda, year, mini month, week and day list and stacked months views or a timeline. Column references are column ids of the same grid: start, end, recurrenceId and seriesEnd are date-and-time columns; allDay, resource, recurrence, exceptions, series, display, description, tone, source and editable.allowedResources are text columns; title, subtitle and status may be any kind. series and recurrenceId go together. A timeline without resources packs the events into rows by overlap; view and phone are views the calendar offers. sources need the source column unless every source has an ics file; create and drop need editable start and title columns; occurrence this and following need series and recurrenceId; validRange starts before it ends. Absent settings keep their defaults.

view.description: The first view; default the first of views.

views.description: Views offered in this order; default month, week, day, agenda, plus timeline with resources.

date.description: The first date shown, yyyy-MM-dd; default today in the display zone.

days.description: Length of the days view; default 3.

firstDay.description: First weekday, 0 (Sunday) to 6; default the page language's.

slotMinutes.description: Time slot size of the week and day views; default 30.

minTime.description: First visible hour, on a slot boundary; default 00:00.

maxTime.description: End of the visible hours, on a slot boundary, after minTime; default 24:00.

scrollTime.description: First hour scrolled into view; default 08:00.

workingHours.description: Working hours; slots outside them are shaded. days default Monday to Friday.

nowIndicator.description: A line at the current time; default true.

eventLimit.description: Events per month cell before +N more; default auto.

timeZone.description: Display zone: utc, local or an IANA zone name; default the grid's timeZone.

editable.description: Moving and resizing events; absent is read-only. move, resize, resources and overlap default true, workingHours false, snapMinutes slotMinutes, commit auto.

resources.description: Resources of the timeline: a complete tree view document (inline roots or a remote source) whose node ids are resource ids.

capacity.description: A concurrency lane for resource groups; thresholds rise.

ranges.description: Static background ranges; end after start.

inverse.description: Shades everything outside the union of the inverse ranges of the same resource (or of those without a resource); default false.

availability.description: Business hours per resource (no resource = every resource); days default Monday to Friday.

limit.description: Most occurrences one range shows; default 20000.

phone.description: The view phones start in; default agenda when offered.

sources.description: Event sources with a legend that switches each off; ids are unique.

ics.description: A relative or same-origin http(s) URL of an iCalendar file whose events join the calendar read-only.

toolbar.description: Grid toolbar controls above the calendar: true (all), false (calendar chrome only) or only those listed; default true.

details.description: What activating an event opens; default drawer.

create.description: Creating events by clicking, dragging and from the keyboard; absent is off. minutes default 60, allDay default true.

occurrence.description: What moving or resizing an occurrence changes; default ask with series and recurrenceId, else all.

navLinks.description: Day names and numbers open that day; default true.

validRange.description: Dates navigation, selection, creation and drops stay inside: start inclusive, end exclusive.

fixedWeeks.description: The month always shows six weeks; default false.

outsideDays.description: The month shows the days of the months around it; default true.

span.description: The timeline's span instead of the zoom's default.

hover.description: A hover card with an event's details; default true.

yearEvents.description: The year view lists each day's events; default false.

agendaSpan.description: The period of the agenda; default month.

months.description: Months of the stacked months view; default 6.

print.description: A Print button that prints the current view; default false.

gridTransaction.description: Changes a host sends to an open flat grid: add (complete rows; a row whose id the grid has replaces it), update (rows whose cells merge into the existing row's; a null cell clears it) and remove (row ids). Removes apply first, then adds, then updates; at most 100,000 rows in all.

gridRowDetail.description: A record's detail row payload in a reporting grid with detail rows: a table, properties or trusted HTML, or the inline data of the definition's nested grid (rows) or tree (roots).

gridDetail.description: Expandable detail rows. At most one content source: a page template id, a plugin detail renderer, or a nested grid or tree view whose data comes from each record's detail payload; none uses each record's own payload.

print.description: Whether exports and print snapshots carry detail payloads. Default true.

aggregate.description: A declared aggregate whose value orders this level's groups (missing values last, ties by value).

gridRowData.description: Compact rows of an inline grid in place of rows: each row an array of its id (or { id, tone, className }) and its cells in the order of columns, without trailing empty cells, in chunks the runtime decodes one at a time. chunks is the number of application/x-canopyx-rows scripts inside the host element (or of sidecar files rows/<n>.js under base), or the chunks themselves: arrays of rows, or with encoding gzip base64 text of the gzip-compressed JSON of each chunk. ordered declares ordinal string order, preserving version-1 reader compatibility. The current runtime answers early windows only when this order also matches display identity order.

gridFormatPredicate.description: A formatting test: a filter predicate with more operators, value types, case sensitivity and a culture, or a comparison with another column.

gridFormatCondition.description: A formatting condition: a filter group with a third junction, none. Eight levels, 64 groups and 64 predicates at most.

gridFormatIcon.description: auto, none, a named icon (up, down, check, cross, warning, info, dot, circle, triangle, square, diamond, flag, star, minus, plus, clock) or up to four characters.

gridFormatRule.description: A conditional formatting rule: identity, condition (absent matches every row), target and style. The first rule that sets an aspect of a target wins it.

searchHighlight.description: Marks search and filter matches inside cells with <mark>, with a match count and next/previous navigation. true uses the defaults. The reader's switch is saved in state.

enabled.description: Marks shown when the view opens. Default true.

filters.description: Mark the values a flat grid's column filters match, styled apart from search hits. Default true.

matchCase.description: Compare case exactly when marking. Default false.

ignoreAccents.description: A letter with accents matches its base letter when marking. Default false.

minLength.description: The shortest term that is marked. Default 1.

filterTones.description: A tone per column id for its filter hits.

layoutOptions.description: A Layout menu with the layout modes and densities the reader can choose; the choice is saved in state.

mode.description: The starting layout; one of modes. Default fit, or the first of modes.

modes.description: The layouts offered, in menu order. Default every layout the view supports.

density.description: The starting density. Default the view's own density.

treeLayoutOptions.description: A tree's Layout menu: the fit and scroll layouts and the densities.

grid.description: A flat data-grid definition. All columns contain cells; none represents hierarchy.

rowIdentity.description: Default stableKey. Ordinal IDs are source positions in one dataset snapshot; saved selections and keyed live updates are unavailable.

autoRowHeight.description: Measure record heights; rowHeight supplies the minimum and unseen-row estimate.

dragRows.description: Rows can be dragged out of the grid (to a calendar that accepts drops) and picked up with F2 from row focus; default false.

zebra.description: Optional alternate-row backgrounds; off by default.

toolbar.description: Per-control toolbar switches; an absent switch keeps its control. A control switched off is not built. The search box is the search property.

exportFormats.description: Identities of browser-registered export formats the Export menu offers after CSV, in order; an identity the page does not register is skipped. Absent offers every registered format.

rowAction.description: What a plain row click does; a plain click never selects. Default none.

editing.description: How editable columns edit (docs/editing.md); a browser host's editing option overrides these.

readOnly.description: The whole grid is read-only until the host calls setReadOnly(false).

mode.description: One cell at a time, or every editable cell of a row. Default cell.

drawer.description: When the record drawer becomes an edit form. Default phone.

editBar.description: The toolbar shows unsaved changes with Undo, Redo, Discard and Save. Default true.

autoHeight.description: A grid whose rows fit is as tall as its rows; false keeps the host height. Default true.

rowAccents.description: Draw a row tone as a bar at the row start. Default false.

formatRules.description: Conditional formatting rules in priority order (docs/conditional-formatting.md).

formatting.description: A legend of the labelled rules and the rule editor in the more menu.

pager.description: Pager settings of a paged grid, read by the pager part; continuous grids ignore them. An absent setting keeps the built-in pager.

lengths.description: Page-size choices in menu order; all (every row) needs an inline source. Absent keeps 10, 25, 50, 100 and All.

numbers.description: Numbered page buttons: 0 for none (default), or 5 to 15.

pageInput.description: The page number field. Absent shows it unless numbered pages show.

firstLast.description: The first-page and last-page buttons. Default true.

info.description: The result text: the compact range (default), a sentence with the unfiltered total while filtered, or none.

searchDelayMs.description: Search-input debounce; absent uses zero for inline sources and 300 for hosted sources. Enter applies immediately.

searchColumns.$comment: Every identity must bind to a declared grid column; absent searches every declared column.

columnGroups.description: Header rows above the columns, up to three levels. Each column belongs to one group at most; the grid keeps a group's columns together in its column order. Loads the column-groups part.

enabled.description: False keeps the API without pointer, keyboard and touch input. Default true.

multiple.description: Ctrl or Cmd adds ranges. Default true.

fillHandle.description: Show the fill handle on a single range. Default false.

rangeSelection.description: Cell ranges by mouse, keyboard and touch, the cell menu and the clipboard keys. Loads the cell-range part. Absent or false leaves them off.

copyHeaders.description: Copies start with the column titles and group rows. Default false.

copyValues.description: Copy the shown text or raw values. Default display.

paste.description: Paste into the cells. Default true.

clipboard.description: How cell ranges copy and paste.

navigation.description: Known-count offset access or paged host cursor traversal. Absent preserves offset access.

gridFacetQuery.$comment: The target must be opted in by reporting.facetColumns. Window and sort do not limit counts. Excluding the current facet replaces its predicates with true; host authorization is preserved.

gridFacetPage.$comment: Runtime checks the request identity/projection/revision, raw column kind, distinct typed canonical buckets and count relations. Without value search a complete response accounts for every matching row, including one missing/null bucket.

gridRangeQuery.description: The records of the complete accepted query that overlap a UTC window [from, to), for calendar and timeline views. Column references name allowed, filterable columns of the view: start, end and seriesEnd are date columns; recurrence and resource are text columns.
gridRangeQuery.$comment: from < to, at most 3,700 days apart. A record without a recurrence (no recurrence column, or a null or empty value) overlaps when start < to and (start >= from or end > from); a null end is a marker at its start. A recurring record overlaps when start < to and, with seriesEnd, its series end is null or after from. resources restricts with in-predicate semantics on the resource column. The query's search, predicates and filter group apply; its window, sort and grouping do not. Servers lower limit to their own maximum; calendarView is informational.

gridRangePage.description: The answer to a gridRangeQuery: the overlapping records ordered by start ascending, then record identity.
gridRangePage.$comment: matched counts every overlapping record after the query's criteria and the resource restriction; items are the first of them (at most the request's limit); truncated is exactly items.length < matched. Revision rules are the gridQuery rules.

rangeInstant.description: An ISO 8601 UTC instant ending in Z; compared at millisecond precision.

gridQuerySelection.description: Ephemeral accepted-query selection. Hosts validate query, revision, count and exclusion membership before acting.

gridState.description: Canonical browser preference snapshot. Runtime binds columns, queries and selection policy to the current definition.

sized.description: The width is a user choice; without it the column keeps automatic sizing.

facets.description: Whether the reader left the facet panel open.

formatRules.description: Formatting rules edited at run time, when they differ from the view's.

gridViewSettings.description: Versioned preference envelope, separate from data authorization and dataset revisions. Serialized envelopes are bounded to 1048576 UTF-16 code units.
gridViewSettings.$comment: Runtime checks unique trimmed names, owning view, default membership and current definition compatibility. Legacy session envelopes without version/view remain readable.

gridReporting.description: Optional capabilities requiring the reporting entry point. Policies bind to declared sortable text columns.

groupBy.description: Initial runtime grouping levels, outermost first. Not combined with grouping.

groupable.description: Readers can group by sortable columns. Not combined with grouping.

anyOf.description: A custom aggregate a browser plugin computes for inline data and a host source for its own.

format.description: Explicit value format; otherwise the column format applies, except that counts default to whole numbers.

gridNumberFormat.description: Display format of binary64 numbers. Defaults are minimum 0 and maximum 3. Minimum must not exceed maximum, so a minimum above 3 requires an explicit maximum. Halfway values round away from zero; literal prefixes follow the sign.

gridSummary.$comment: Readers validate exact view/revision/query ownership, aggregate bindings, contiguous groups accounting for matched records and a 4194304-code-unit envelope bound. Grouping requires known-count offset navigation.

groups.description: The next level's groups inside this group; present on every group of an outer level and absent on the innermost.

gridColumnLayout.$comment: Writers/readers require minimum <= initial column width <= maximum. Runtime state preserves base width and flex-enabled intent separately from viewport allocation.

oneOf.description: A summary of a structured value (a list, object, collection, timeline or changes): a count, chips, or the first item and +N.

categories.$comment: Writers and readers also reject category collisions after the selected frozen case folding.

gridPage.description: A page after full-dataset filtering and sorting. Writers and readers check offset <= matched <= total, page bounds, and unique row identities.

gridQuery.description: Search, AND-combined flat predicates and the optional nested filter group precede ordered sorting and paging. Missing values sort last; row identity breaks final ties.

groupBy.description: Runtime grouping levels of a definition with groupBy or groupable, always present for such definitions; their columns lead sort.

gridCursorPage.description: A complete visible page reached through opaque host cursors. Offset is the actual ordinal position; unknown counts are null. Readers enforce contiguous navigation, consistent revisions/counts, page bounds and unique identities.

gridCursor.$comment: Runtime and writer enforce the limit in UTF-16 code units and reject malformed Unicode.

gridCursorQuery.description: The same full-dataset query criteria as gridQuery, traversed through an optional opaque cursor; no random-access offset is sent.

gridFilterGroup.description: A nonempty AND/OR group. Readers enforce eight levels, 64 groups and 64 predicates total, including flat query predicates.

tone.description: neutral, info, success, warning, danger, muted, or a tone the host theme defines.

cell.description: A bare value, or an object with a value plus display text, tooltip, tone, and badges.

searchText.description: Alternate flat-grid search text; it does not change display, sort, filter or export values.

items.description: A list value: items shown as chips. At most one of items, fields, records, events and changes; writers and readers enforce it, and that list items are values.

fields.description: An object value: named values shown as a nested property list.

events.description: A timeline value, in the order shown.

sort.description: Sort key when it differs from the value (orthogonal sort data); filters, value lists, search and display keep reading value and text.

height.description: Row slots the detail row spans; without it the row is as tall as its content.

widths.description: Column widths as shares of the table width, one per column.

data.description: Host facts handed to host callbacks; not shown and not searched.

fields.description: Values of the view's record fields (record.fields), shown in the record drawer only.

childCount.$comment: When children is present, readers require this value to equal its length; this cross-field equality is a semantic protocol constraint.

wrap.description: Wrap flat-grid cell text within its width.

autoWidth.description: Tree columns: fit the visible rows' content; width is the fallback until the tree tools part measures.

fixed.description: Tree columns: the width is hard during fitting. Otherwise width is preferred.

flex.description: Tree columns: share of spare width, given before the tree column.

autoSize.description: Tree columns: what content measuring reads. Default content.

alwaysVisible.description: Tree columns: retained during responsive fitting.

pinned.description: The tree column pins left by default and null lets it scroll; other columns pin left (after the tree column) or right.

drawer.description: false keeps the column out of the tree's record drawer. Default true.

section.description: The record drawer section of a tree column.

renderer.description: The name of a cell renderer a browser plugin registers (cellRenderers, docs/plugins.md). An unregistered name keeps the built-in painter; a host renderer for the column wins.

gridColumnGroup.description: A named group of columns drawn as a header above them. It lists the columns directly below it and its nested groups.

columns.$comment: Every identity binds to a declared grid column, in one group at most.

groups.$comment: At most three levels of groups.

pinned.description: Initial pin of every column of a top-level group; null scrolls. Nested groups take none.

autoWidth.description: Fit loaded content on first layout. Width remains a numeric fallback; saved widths take precedence.

filterable.description: Supports query predicates and filter controls. Default true; supported read-only facets and presentation rules remain available.

exportable.description: Supports grid exports. Default true. Default exports omit false; explicit requests reject it.

editable.description: Readers can edit the column's cells; the editing part loads with the grid (docs/editing.md).

format.description: Number columns only: display format of raw numbers without cell text, also used by summaries and selection totals.

drawer.description: false keeps the column out of the record drawer and record panel. Default true.

maxWidth.description: Widest width and the content measuring cap.

alwaysVisible.description: Retain this column during responsive fitting. Explicit user hiding still applies.

tooltip.description: auto shows a cell's full value on hover while it is cut off; another value names a declared column whose text the tooltip shows.

fixed.description: The width is hard; requires width. Otherwise width is preferred.

flex.description: Share of spare width, given before the identity column.

autoSize.description: What content measuring reads. Default content.

priority.description: How the column gives way when narrow. Integers follow responsivePriority: 0-1 essential, 10000+ optional.

pinned.description: Requested edge; null unpins. The identity column pins left by default.

rowHeader.description: The identity column; defaults to the first column. At most one.

quietTones.description: Tones an enum or state presenter shows as plain muted text.

queryAware.description: The host applies the view query before paging; every page carries a dataset revision.

hidden.description: The toolbar draws no switch; the host controls the filter.

dragDrop.description: Offers proposals to a host drop hook; the runtime never moves nodes itself.

checkboxes.description: Checking is independent of row selection; hierarchical rules include unloaded descendants.

checkIntents.$comment: Writers and readers also require unique paths when checked values differ; JSON Schema uniqueItems compares complete items.

kinds.description: The node kinds search can find; every node when absent.

timeZone.description: The time zone datetime columns show at first; utc when absent.

pinTreeColumn.description: The tree column stays in view while the other columns scroll sideways.

toolbar.description: Per-control tree toolbar switches; an absent switch keeps its control. A control switched off is not built. The search box is the search property.

autoHeight.description: A tree whose visible rows fit is as tall as its rows; false keeps the host height. Default true.

labels.description: Translations of the texts the runtime writes itself; English where a name is absent. {placeholders} are replaced.

viewQuery.description: JSON carried in the viewQuery URL parameter; it is not a document envelope.

counts.$comment: Counts item ids are unique within a document; writers and readers enforce this semantic constraint.

packs.description: The number of p/<n> pack files. When present, a reference p/<n>#<slot> names page <slot> of pack <n>.

entryFiles.description: The number of the first entry in each e/<n> file, in file order.

shards.description: Each shard file's key and the number of entries its posting lists refer to.

entryPacks.description: With shardPacks: the index is packed into q/<n> files. The number of the first entry file in each entry pack, in pack order, starting with 0.

shardPacks.description: The first shard key, in ordinal order, of each shard pack; shard packs follow the entry packs.

pages.description: In a p/<n> pack, the children pages of many nodes, each as the JSON text of a page document; in a q/<n> pack, the search entry files or shards of an index, each as the JSON text of its document. A reader parses only the one it needs.

shardKey.description: A prefix of at least two encoded code units, with a trailing - for the word exactly that long, or one encoded code unit and - for a one-unit word; numbered parts append .2, .3, and so on.

postings.description: One list per word. A list starts with an entry number; after it a positive value is the gap to the next entry and a negative value -n stands for the n entries that follow without a gap.

searchEntry.description: [parent entry number or -1, leading code units shared with the parent id, id part, trailing code units shared with the parent id, label, kind number or null, reference of the first children page when it is in another file than the page that holds the node, or null; reference of the page that holds the node when it is in another file than the first page of its list]; trailing nulls are left out.

recordRef.description: A link to another record: of the value's own view, or of the grid or tree with id view. path is a tree record's id path, ending with id.

recordList.description: A collection of records: rows with their own columns (or tree roots), the total when rows are the first ones, and the grid whose records they are.

recordPanel.description: The record panel: record-only fields, a pinned summary, sections, tabs, empty-field hiding, jump list, record deep links, where details load from and the built-in actions. docs/record-panel.md. Writers and readers check that ids are unique and that sections, tabs and the summary name declared fields and sections.

gridRecordQuery.description: A request for one record's details when its drawer opens: the whole record, the next rows of a collection field (field, offset, limit), or with row the record's row too.

gridRecord.description: One record's details: record field values, fuller column values for the drawer, and the row when asked for it.

gridRecordPack.description: A record pack beside a page (records/r<shard>.js): the details of the records whose id hashes to the shard (FNV-1a of the UTF-16 code units, modulo the shard count).

stem.description: The ancestors of the first entry from the top level down, each as its entry number followed by the fields of an entry.
